claims.text: The AWSx ELB component integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC to give compute in AWS configurable network accessibility.
The AWSx ELB component provisions Application and Network Load Balancers.
The example load balancer listens on port 80 in the account's per-region default VPC using its public subnets, exposing it to the internet.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
Targeting an EC2 instance with the load balancer involves five steps (the list shows four numbered items after renumbering).
LaunchTemplate is documented in the Pulumi AWS registry API docs at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/.
AWSx uses the target group passed in the task definition's portMappings to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw aws.ecs requires manual security group rule management.
The example program exports a stack output named `url` that serves the endpoint.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive for ECS: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
Pulumi recommends ALBs for ECS services unless a service requires a feature only available with NLBs.
By default, a load balancer is created as internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
Load balancers accept either a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs).
NLBs support protocols TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC, while ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP and ALBs choose HTTP or HTTPS based on port.
The `listener` property chooses smart defaults based on whether the listener is created against a load balancer or a target group.
The AWS docs URLs rule-action-types.html#fixed-response-actions, #redirect-actions, and listener-rules.html exist and cover these topics.
deregistrationDelay range is 0–3600 seconds and default is 300.
slowStart range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable; disabled by default.
Stickiness is available for ALBs only.
targetType possible values are instance, ip, lambda, and alb; default is instance; IPs must be within VPC private range, RFC 1918 ranges, or RFC 6598 range 100.64.0.0/10.
healthCheck interval range is 5–300 seconds with default 30.
healthyThreshold range is 2–10 with default 3.
unhealthyThreshold range is 2–10, default 3, and for NLBs must equal healthyThreshold.
healthCheck timeout range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
HTTP/2 is not supported for NLBs.
